definitions.explanation: A mythical creature from Japanese folklore said to inhabit rivers and ponds. Typically depicted as humanoid with a turtle-like shell, webbed hands and feet, and a dish-shaped depression on top of its head that holds water, which is the source of its power.

examples.japanese: {河童|かっぱ}は{川|かわ}や{池|いけ}に{住|す}むと{言|い}われている。
examples.english: Kappa are said to live in rivers and ponds.

examples.japanese: {河童|かっぱ}の{頭|あたま}の{皿|さら}が{乾|かわ}くと{力|ちから}が{抜|ぬ}けるらしい。
examples.english: Apparently when the dish on a kappa's head dries out, it loses its strength.

examples.japanese: {河童|かっぱ}の{川流|かわなが}れ
examples.english: Even kappa get swept away by rivers (even experts can fail at their specialty)

notes:
PHYSICAL CHARACTERISTICS:
・{皿|さら} (dish/plate) on top of head - holds water that gives them power
・{緑色|みどりいろ}の{肌|はだ} (green skin)
・{甲羅|こうら} (turtle shell)
・{水|みず}かき (webbed hands and feet)
・{嘴|くちばし} (beak-like mouth)

FOLKLORE:
・Said to love cucumbers ({胡瓜|きゅうり})
・Known for pulling people into water
・Will politely return a bow (causing water to spill from their dish)
・Associated with {相撲|すもう} (sumo wrestling)

PROVERBS:
・{河童|かっぱ}の{川流|かわなが}れ (even experts make mistakes)
・{河童|かっぱ}に{水練|すいれん} (teaching a fish to swim - unnecessary instruction)

CULTURAL PRESENCE:
・{遠野|とおの} in Iwate Prefecture is famous for kappa folklore
・{河童|かっぱ}{寿司|ずし} (cucumber roll) is named after their favorite food
・Featured in many anime, manga, and video games

SIMILAR CREATURES:
・{天狗|てんぐ} (tengu) - mountain goblin
・{座敷童|ざしきわらし} (zashiki-warashi) - house spirit
